security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, when Smcdeleg/Ssccfg delegates mcyclecfg/minstretcfg to S-mode, the kernel's context switch path (sys/riscv/riscv/swtch.S) does not save/restore these CSRs, allowing a thread to program mcyclecfg.___INH bits so that cycle/instret counters selectively skip counting during target execution, leaking timing information.
security_spec.summary: Smcntrpmf mcyclecfg/minstretcfg INH bits must be context-switched per thread, otherwise a thread can reprogram counter inhibition to time kernel or other processes via rdcycle/rdinstret

findings.finding: cpu_switch saves/restores GPRs (ra, sp, s0-s11) and FPE state, but does NOT save/restore mcyclecfg/minstretcfg/mcyclecfgh/minstretcfgh. When Smcdeleg delegates these CSRs from M-mode to S-mode, a thread setting ___INH bits in mcyclecfg will persist across context switches, selectively suppressing cycle/instret counting for subsequent threads. This leaks timing information across thread boundaries.

cpu_throw (initial thread activation path) loads GPRs and optionally FPE state but does not initialize or sanitize mcyclecfg/minstretcfg for the new thread. A newly spawned thread inherits whatever filtering configuration the previous thread left in these CSRs.
findings.snippet:
ENTRY(cpu_throw)
	call	_C_LABEL(pmap_activate_sw)
	/* Loads GPRs, optionally FPE; no mcyclecfg/minstretcfg init */
	ret

findings.finding: struct pcb has no fields for mcyclecfg, minstretcfg, mcyclecfgh, or minstretcfgh. Without per-thread storage, the context-switch path has nowhere to save/restore these CSRs. This is a structural gap: even if swtch.S were updated, the PCB lacks the necessary slots.

encoding.h defines scounteren (CSR_SCOUNTEREN, 0x106) and mcounteren (CSR_MCOUNTEREN, 0x306) but has NO definitions for mcyclecfg (0x321), minstretcfg (0x322), mcyclecfgh (0x721), or minstretcfgh (0x722). These CSRs are completely absent from FreeBSD's kernel headers, making any save/restore code impossible to write without first adding the definitions.

vmm_switch atomically swaps sstatus, hstatus, scounteren, sscratch, stvec between host and guest but does NOT handle mcyclecfg/minstretcfg. If the host kernel sets ___INH bits, a guest VM exit does not restore host configuration. Conversely, a guest VM (if it could access these CSRs through nested virtualization) could poison the host's counter filtering state.
findings.snippet:
csrrw	t0, sstatus, t0
csrrw	t1, hstatus, t1
csrrw	t2, scounteren, t2
csrrw	t3, sscratch, a0
csrrw	t4, stvec, t4
/* mcyclecfg/minstretcfg NOT swapped */
